ground_truth.title: Top 5 Mailchimp alternatives to consider in 2026
ground_truth.author: Maryna Shulzhenko
ground_truth.main_content:
TL;DR

While Mailchimp once dominated due to affordability, its growing limitations are driving many users to consider more capable alternatives.

Users often switch from Mailchimp because of inefficient billing model, limited automation capabilities, deliverability issues, and slow support.

Top 5 Mailchimp alternatives to consider in 2026 include Maropost Marketing Cloud, Omnisend, Klaviyo, ActiveCampaign, and Moosend, offering better value for money.

Maropost Marketing Cloud delivers higher deliverability, deeper insights, and more scalability than Mailchimp, making it a stronger choice for growing ecommerce brands.

Mailchimp has been around for a while now, helping businesses handle their email marketing needs. And for a good reason. With its affordable pricing, it was the top email marketing platform of choice for many small to medium-sized businesses. But it isn’t the right email marketing software for everyone.

If Mailchimp’s limited automation and customization options, deliverability issues, inefficient pricing model, and customer support challenges have you searching for alternatives – you’re definitely not alone. Fortunately, there are plenty of other options that are worth exploring.

In this blog, we’ll walk you through the top 5 best Mailchimp alternatives worth your attention in 2026, pointing out their key capabilities, strengths and weaknesses, and ideal use cases. On top of that, we’ll show you how Maropost Marketing Cloud stacks up against Mailchimp and why it might be just the right email marketing automation software for your needs.

NB: The information below is accurate as of January 2026.

Why should you consider a Mailchimp alternative?

There might be various reasons why users might choose to step away and look for alternative email services like Mailchimp. So first things first, let’s take a look at the most common ones (based on user reviews):

Pricing and billing structure: Mailchimp has increased its pricing several times over the past years, often without adding significant new value. As of today, it can be up to 6x more expensive than its alternatives. Beyond that, costs can quickly start to add up as your contact list grows because Mailchimp charges you for every contact, including duplicates across multiple lists, inactive contacts, and unsubscribed users.

Limited automation: While Mailchimp does offer basic automation tools, it falls short for businesses needing more advanced automation capabilities like behavior-based triggers, multi-step workflows, dynamic landing pages, and advanced A/B testing tools.

Deliverability issues: With Mailchimp, users often face deliverability issues (i.e., emails landing in spam/ promotions rather than inboxes). Based on independent research, Mailchimp’s email deliverability rates have varied from 82% to 95% over the past decade. This suggests that nearly 1 in every 10 emails might not reach the intended inbox. Users often attribute Mailchimp’s deliverability problems to shared or overused IPs.

Customer support quality: When it comes to customer support, users have been reporting slow response times and less personalized assistance (especially with lower-tier plans) compared to some Mailchimp competitors. While this may not seem critical at first, for businesses that rely on quick support (e.g., for deliverability issues, contact list problems, or campaign errors), poor support can be a deal-breaker.

1. Maropost Marketing Cloud

Maropost Marketing Cloud is an ecommerce marketing automation platform. It makes a compelling Mailchimp alternative for mid-market ecommerce and retail merchants, especially for those that have outgrown the “starter kit” stage and need deeper automation, better deliverability, and more scalability. Where Mailchimp is often praised for being great for basic newsletters or small-list campaigns, Maropost is designed to support large-scale email and multichannel marketing. On top of that, with Maropost’s eRFM reporting, you can segment customers by value and engagement to deliver more personalized, retention-driving campaigns.

Key features:

Cross-channel campaigns (emails+SMS+Meta ads)

Unlimited users, contacts, lists, and journeys with the Enterprise plan

Dynamic landing pages + a drag-and-drop page builder

AI-powered product recommendations

Send-time and conversion-time optimization

Advanced customer segmentation with eRFM reporting

A/B testing campaigns

One-click third-party integrations

Access to a dedicated deliverability support team

24/7 chat support across all plans

Pros Cons
Cross-channel campaigns (email, SMS, Meta ads) Unified view of customer data across all channels Advanced eRFM analytics and custom reporting No free plan, might not be suitable for small businesses Less ideal for business that need just basic email automation Longer setup and steeper learning curve

Best for: Mid-market to enterprise-grade ecommerce and retail brands, high-volume senders, businesses needing complex, multi-channel marketing orchestration.

2. Omnisend

Omnisend is an email marketing software built specifically for ecommerce businesses. It combines email, SMS, and push notifications into unified workflows and offers lots of built-in ecommerce features (like dynamic product recommendations and discount-code insertion). Compared to Mailchimp, Omnisend delivers more value for online stores: its automation and multi-channel capabilities are more advanced by default, and even free/entry-level plans unlock segmentation and ecommerce-specific automations.

Key features:

Unlimited monthly emails with higher-tier plans

Cross-channel campaigns (email+SMS+push notifications)

Popups, signup forms, and landing pages

Behavior-based segmentation

Contact list cleaning tool

Sales and performance reporting

Pre-built integrations and APIs

24/7 live chat and email support

Pros Cons
Quick setup and beginner-friendly automation Omnichannel integration (email, SMS, push notifications) Advanced ecommerce-specific automations Less suited for non-ecommerce businesses Pricing can scale quickly with SMS usage No custom reporting options

Best for: Small to mid-sized ecommerce brands looking for a budget-friendly ecommerce email marketing tool.

3. Klaviyo

Klaviyo is also built specifically for ecommerce businesses. It offers advanced segmentation, event-triggered automation, and predictive analytics that let you send highly personalized email/ SMS campaigns based on customer behavior. Unlike Mailchimp’s basic reporting, Klaviyo provides stronger insights into revenue, customer lifetime value, and lifecycle-based marketing performance, making it a better choice for growing online stores that care about ROI.

4. ActiveCampaign

Compared to Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign is a more full-featured and advanced platform that actually goes beyond marketing automation. It combines email marketing, advanced segmentation, and an integrated CRM, letting you build complex, behavior-driven customer journeys, trigger cross-channel messages, and do lead scoring and deal tracking in one place. Ultimately, this makes ActiveCampaign more expensive than Mailchimp, but also significantly better for businesses that want more flexibility and scalability.

5. Moosend

Moosend is a budget-friendly email marketing platform that gives many of the essentials you’d expect from a larger system. Compared to Mailchimp, Moosend often wins on affordability and simplicity. Its drag-and-drop builder, basic automation workflows, list segmentation, and reporting make it especially attractive for small businesses or marketers new to email campaigns. Moosend is a great fit if you want straightforward email marketing – it’s easy to set up, easy to run, and cost-effective.

Maropost Marketing Cloud vs Mailchimp: what’s the right solution for your business?

Mailchimp might be one of the most recognized names in the email marketing industry – but it isn’t the right tool for everyone, especially for growing businesses. Here’s a more detailed overview of how it compares to Maropost Marketing Cloud to help you decide between the two platforms.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: pricing model

Mailchimp’s pricing model charges per contact (even duplicates or inactive ones), which can become pretty costly as your list grows. It basically means that if one customer appears in two different lists, you’ll have to pay twice. With Maropost Marketing Cloud, you pay for the emails you send – not for how many contacts you store in your database. No wasted spend.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: deliverability

Maropost Marketing Cloud is known for excellent email deliverability. While Mailchimp’s deliverability rate typically ranges between 82% and 95%, Maropost Marketing Cloud ensures a 98% deliverability rate on your email marketing campaigns by using adaptive sending technology, maintaining a high-trust sender environment, providing real-time deliverability analytics, and offering dedicated deliverability support and remediation.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: engagement-based analytics

While Mailchimp does allow you to track basic campaign performance metrics and purchase behavior with the ecommerce integration, Maropost goes a lot further than that. With Maropost’s eRFM reporting, you can see your customers grouped by recency, frequency, and monetary value, as well as their engagement patterns. These insights make it easier for you to target the right groups with specific campaigns and improve personalization and retention.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: scalability

Mailchimp scales well for small to mid-sized businesses. It can comfortably handle growing subscriber lists from a few hundred to tens or even hundreds of thousands. But Maropost Marketing Cloud is built from the ground up for enterprise-level scalability. It can easily handle massive contact databases and high-volume sending without any drop in performance. Maropost’s infrastructure is optimized for speed and deliverability at scale.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: customer support

Users on G2 frequently point out the higher quality of support they receive from Maropost, which holds a 9.0 rating compared to Mailchimp’s 8.0. Many note that Maropost’s responsive and knowledgeable customer service team is a real advantage, especially for businesses that need immediate help.

✔️ Maropost Marketing Cloud vs. Mailchimp: beyond marketing automation

Mailchimp is a solid marketing automation platform, but ultimately, it’s just that – a tool built to help small businesses automate their email and SMS campaigns. Maropost goes far beyond that. Marketing Cloud is part of the Maropost Unified Commerce platform – a solution that lets you run your marketing, ecommerce, merchandising, and customer support from one system – eliminating the chaos of juggling disconnected tools.
